requirements.requirement: Serve a working HTTPS endpoint on node1 port 8443.
requirements.summary: nginx listened on 0.0.0.0:8443, returned the expected response, presented the same certificate stored on disk, and passed hostname/certificate verification using the configured trust anchor. The endpoint also recovered after restart.

requirements.requirement: Automatically renew the certificate before it expires.
requirements.summary: A running, boot-enabled cron service schedules the daily renewal hook. With a certificate deliberately placed inside the seven-day renewal window, that hook replaced it with a new certificate valid for 30 days; a normal run outside the window correctly left it unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Load each renewed certificate while continuing to answer HTTPS requests.
requirements.summary: Both forced and expiry-window rotations changed the certificate serial, nginx immediately served the new serial, and each bounded concurrent probe completed 120/120 successful requests with no failures.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, a different boot ID appeared, and the HTTPS service, certificate, scheduler, and policy recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the reboot.
limitations: The daily hook was exercised directly under an induced expiry condition rather than by waiting for the 02:00 cron invocation; the active crond service and exact schedule make the automation evidence strong but not a wall-clock scheduler observation.
Alpine does not support the collector's systemd failed-unit probe, so that snapshot cannot independently enumerate failed OpenRC services.
Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory certificate release directories, so they cannot determine whether older generated certificate releases constitute intentional rollback history or residue.

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation was generally disciplined, and package consistency remained unchanged. Two retained hygiene issues were observed: nginx unnecessarily exposed its default HTTP service on ports 80/IPv4 and 80/IPv6 after installation and startup (cmd-70d7b045afbf4ab8, cmd-bf3d06106ad6408f), and three test artifacts remained in /tmp: rotation-probe.log from cmd-d0d1766b30a44d45 plus scheduled-rotation-probe.log and short-cert-result from cmd-59af394229224f8d. None was reverted or cleaned. The temporary one-day certificate policy mutation in cmd-59af394229224f8d was evidence-related and fully restored, so it is not penalized.
